design.data_generating_process: continuous Gaussian trait with species-specific baseline linked to geographic species centre plus a signed within-species local linear effect whose sign is reversed in a fixed fraction of species

comparators: one-sided one-sample test on species-specific distance-dissimilarity rho
analytic DerSimonian-Laird random-effects summary of species-specific signed slopes
within-species permutation-calibrated random-effects signed-slope mean/Q omnibus

interpretation.supported: Species-specific signed slopes can represent direction heterogeneity, but the usual analytic random-effects mean and Q approximations are anti-conservative in this small-sample/missingness design. Recalibrating the same slope/meta statistics by within-species matched trait permutations restores the combined omnibus to a maximum null rejection fraction of 0.05 and retains substantial power for opposing species-specific directions. This provides a flexible signed-slope complement to the direction-invariant distance-dissimilarity estimand rather than a universally superior replacement.
not_supported: analytic DerSimonian-Laird p-values are calibrated for small per-species samples
the individual calibrated mean and heterogeneity component tests are each guaranteed to stay below 0.05 in every finite benchmark cell
random-effects slope meta-analysis is universally superior to matched distance-dissimilarity inference
the calibrated slope-meta omnibus and distance-dissimilarity omnibus estimate the same biological quantity
this benchmark validates nonlinear, multivariate or MNAR settings
